summary: The chartered East India companies of the 1600s-1800s: the Dutch company depopulated the Banda Islands to monopolise nutmeg, and the British company under Robert Clive seized Bengal, where its taxation drove the famine of 1770 that killed millions.

evidence.note: British company chartered at the end of 1600; covered span starts here
Dutch admiral sails to the Banda Islands in 1609, first violent episode; main span starts
Coen depopulates the Bandas, shipping survivors to Batavia as slaves; most of the population dies
Long Robert Clive segment begins, running into part 2 up to his death in 1774
Plassey victory hands the company Bengal
Bengal famine of 1769-1773 and the company's role in it, the main harm of the story
First regulation of the company in 1784 after repeated famines; main span ends
Afghan invasion and rout, then the 1858 crown takeover of India; covered span ends
Clive's suicide and its method described

notes: Title names one company; the British company gets most airtime and the host names it the most notable, so it is primary and the Dutch company (about a third of the story) is secondary. Bengal maps to IN and BD. The 1874 dissolution is a one-line mention, so covered span ends at 1858. Polities list has no Mughal or Dutch empire entry.
